title: What the dated ZPC (Posture Control) release upgrade summary notes for 2022 and 2023 say

prose.text: Whether the limited-availability features reached general availability is open {{gap:limited-availability-outcome}}. The policy and service tables are not recorded {{gap:policy-and-service-tables}}. Values the notes do not give are open {{gap:unstated-values}}. The IaC time filter names are open {{gap:time-filter-names}}.

aws-windows-2022-12.statement: The December 08, 2022 note says agentless vulnerability scanning of AWS Windows workloads is supported, for Windows Server 2016, 2019 and 2022.

quotes: #### December 08, 2022
The agentless vulnerability scanning of Amazon Web Services (AWS) Windows workloads is supported. The following Windows server versions are supported: 2016, 2019, and 2022.

azure-windows-2022-10.statement: The October 13, 2022 note says agentless vulnerability scanning of Azure Windows workloads is supported, for Windows Server 2016, 2019 and 2022.

quotes: The agentless vulnerability scanning of Azure Windows workloads is supported. The following Windows server versions are supported: 2016, 2019, and 2022.

aws-keys-amis-2022-10.statement: The October 13, 2022 note says vulnerability scanning can be performed on AWS managed keys encrypted volumes as well as Customer Managed Keys encrypted volumes, and is supported for Linux workloads created from AWS marketplace AMIs except appliance AMIs.

quotes: You can perform vulnerability scanning on Amazon Web Services (AWS) managed keys encrypted volumes, in addition to Customer Managed Keys (CMKs) encrypted volumes.
The vulnerability scanning for Linux workloads that are created using AWS marketplace Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) is supported, except appliance AMIs.

azure-linux-2022-09.statement: The September 06, 2022 note says vulnerability scanning of Azure Linux workloads is supported with limited availability, and that scanning can be enabled for specific instances and scheduled at regular intervals.

quotes: #### September 06, 2022
Vulnerability scanning of Azure Linux workloads is supported with limited availability.
You can enable the vulnerability scanning for specific instances within the cloud workload and schedule the scan to run at regular intervals.

gcp-workloads-2023-03.statement: The March 01, 2023 note says ZPC supports agentless vulnerability scanning of Linux and Windows GCP workloads, both non-encrypted and encrypted with Google-managed encryption.

quotes: ZPC supports the agentless vulnerability scanning of both Linux and Windows Google Cloud Platform (GCP) workloads.
ZPC supports the vulnerability scanning of both non-encrypted and encrypted (Google-managed encryption) workloads.

default-weekly-2023-09.statement: The September 13, 2023 note says the default scan schedule for cloud workloads is set to weekly and can be switched to daily.

quotes: #### September 13, 2023
The default scan schedule is set to weekly for cloud workloads. The scan schedule can be switched to daily if required.

failed-scan-errors-2023.statement: The January 19, 2023 note says a workload or container image not scanned because of an internal or permission error shows scan status Failed with an error message in the ZPC Admin Portal; the September 13, 2023 note says scan errors related to insufficient privileges or missing cloud resources are shown on the Notification Center page.

quotes: #### September 13, 2023
Whenever a cloud workload or container image is not scanned due to an internal or permission error
the scan status is displayed as Failed along with the relevant error message on the ZPC Admin Portal.
Information about vulnerability scan errors related to insufficient privileges or missing cloud resources are displayed on the Notification Center page in the ZPC Admin Portal.

gar-2023-05.statement: The May 17, 2023 note says ZPC supports scanning container images in Google Artifact Registry, in addition to the previous support for Google Container Registry, and says GCR is expected to be deprecated in the near future.

quotes: ZPC provides support for scanning container images stored in the Google Artifact Registry (GAR). This is in addition to the previous support for scanning container images in the Google Container Registry (GCR).
GCR is expected to be deprecated in the near future and GAR is going to be the default registry for container images and packages.

compute-gallery-2023-06.statement: The June 19, 2023 note says ZPC supports scanning workload images created in Azure Compute Gallery, where previously only Azure Marketplace images were supported.

quotes: ZPC now provides support for scanning cloud workload images created in Azure Compute Gallery. Previously, ZPC provided support only for scanning workload images in the Azure Marketplace.

ubuntu-amzn-2023.statement: The June 19, 2023 note says ZPC supports detecting vulnerabilities in cloud workloads running Ubuntu 23.04 (Lunar Lobster); the April 19, 2023 note says it supports vulnerability scanning for Amazon Linux 2022 and Amazon Linux 2023.

quotes: ZPC supports the detection of vulnerabilities present in cloud workloads having Ubuntu 23.04 (Lunar Lobster) OS version.
ZPC provides vulnerability scanning support for Amazon Linux 2022 and Amazon Linux 2023 versions.

ms-packages-2023-05.statement: The May 17, 2023 note says ZPC supports detecting vulnerabilities in some Microsoft packages, naming .NET Framework, .NET Core Runtime, .NET Runtime, ASP .NET, Visual Studio, PowerShell and SQL Server Management Studio.

quotes: ZPC supports the detection of vulnerabilities in some of the Microsoft packages such as .NET Framework, .NET Core Runtime, .NET Runtime, ASP .NET, Visual Studio, PowerShell, and SQL Server Management Studio.

container-scanning-2023.statement: Dated 2023 notes say ZPC identifies all active images used by containers in monitored clusters and scans them for vulnerabilities: EKS (March 23, 2023, scanning images present in ECR), GKE (June 19, 2023) and AKS (July 12, 2023).

quotes: ZPC supports the scanning of containers deployed to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) clusters.
ZPC identifies all active images used by containers in monitored Kubernetes clusters and scans the images present in elastic container registries (ECR) for vulnerabilities.
ZPC identifies all active images used by containers in monitored Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters and scans the images for vulnerabilities.
ZPC identifies all active images used by containers in monitored Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters and scans the images for vulnerabilities.

public-exposure-containers-2023-06.statement: The June 19, 2023 note says the Vulnerability Management page can list publicly exposed cloud workloads, and that container status (active or non-active) is shown in the Containers tab with a Running Status filter.

quotes: You can view the list of cloud workloads that are publicly exposed on the Vulnerability Management page.
ZPC displays the status of the containers in the Containers tab on the Vulnerability Management page. You can also apply the Running Status filter to view either the active or non-active containers.

advisories-2023-08.statement: The August 17, 2023 note says ZPC scans cloud assets and provides more information on detected security advisories, with links to details of the threat methods and risks.

quotes: ZPC scans your cloud assets and provides more information on detected security advisories along with accessible links to understand in detail about the threat methods and associated risks.

export-2022-09.statement: The September 06, 2022 note says vulnerability scan results can be exported to an Excel file, and the vulnerabilities of a cloud asset can be viewed and exported.

quotes: #### September 06, 2022
You can export the vulnerability scan results to an Excel file and download the report.
You can view and export the list of all vulnerabilities associated with a cloud asset.

bicep-2022-12.statement: The December 08, 2022 note says IaC supports scanning Bicep files by converting them with the Bicep CLI into JSON (ARM template) files and scanning the JSON.

quotes: #### December 08, 2022
You can use the Bicep CLI to convert Bicep files into JSON files (Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates) and scan the JSON files for misconfigurations and policy violations.

functions-2022-10.statement: The October 13, 2022 note says Zscaler IaC Scan can parse the Date and Numeric functions in ARM templates and the Date, Time and File System functions in Terraform templates.

quotes: The Date and Numeric functions in ARM templates are supported.
The Date, Time, and File System functions in Terraform templates are supported.

arm-2022-09.statement: The September 06, 2022 note says ARM templates and specific functions are fully supported for IaC, with partial support of CIS benchmark compliance coverage.

quotes: #### September 06, 2022
The Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates and specific functions are now fully supported for infrastructure-as-code (IaC), with partial support of CIS benchmark compliance coverage.

terraform-cloud-2022.statement: Dated 2022 notes on Terraform Cloud: September 06, 2022 says the Zscaler IaC Scan app can scan run tasks in Terraform workspaces; October 13, 2022 says Advanced Settings let you select the severity level for failing a build.

quotes: #### September 06, 2022
You can integrate the Zscaler IaC Scan app with Terraform Cloud and scan run tasks in Terraform workspaces.
You can use the Advanced Settings for Terraform Cloud integration and select the severity level for failing a build.

terraform-preplan-2023-01.statement: The January 19, 2023 note says Zscaler IaC Scan supports scanning Terraform Cloud templates during the pre-plan phase, which shows policy violations for specific lines of code.

quotes: Zscaler IaC Scan supports the scanning of Terraform Cloud templates during the pre-plan phase. This option allows you to see policy violations for specific lines of code within the template file.

azure-repos-push-2022-09.statement: The September 06, 2022 note says ZPC supports IaC scanning of push events in Microsoft Azure Repos, triggering a scan on push events.

quotes: #### September 06, 2022
ZPC provides support for the IaC scanning of push events in Microsoft Azure Repos. ZPC triggers a scan on push events and detects misconfigurations and policy violations.

reauth-auth-2022-10.statement: The October 13, 2022 note says IaC integrations with Azure DevOps and GitLab can be reauthorized when authorization expired or the integration was unintentionally revoked, and that Visual Studio Code and CLI authentication launches into the browser and supports users mapped to multiple tenants.

quotes: You can reauthorize the IaC integration with Azure DevOps and GitLab in the event the authorization has expired or if the integration was unintentionally revoked.
Authentication for Visual Studio Code and command-line interface (CLI) now launches into the browser and supports users mapped to multiple tenants.

paths-2023.statement: The January 19, 2023 note says IaC Scan can scan specific directories within a version control repository; the March 01, 2023 note says regex patterns can include or exclude file paths, with the include option under Advanced Settings for GitHub, GitLab and Azure Repos.

quotes: Zscaler IaC Scan now supports the scanning of specific directories within a version control repository.

You can use regular expression (regex) patterns to specify the file paths that must be included or excluded in IaC scans. The option to include the file path is available under Advanced Settings for GitHub, GitLab, and Azure Repos.

secrets-2023-01.statement: The January 19, 2023 note says IaC scanning obfuscates secrets such as access keys and database passwords in Terraform and CloudFormation templates.

quotes: IaC scanning obfuscates secrets such as access keys and database passwords which are present in the Terraform and CloudFormation templates.

scm-ide-2023.statement: Dated 2023 notes add IaC scanning for Bitbucket repositories (April 19, 2023), a Zscaler IaC Scan plugin for JetBrains IDEs (March 23, 2023) and IaC CI/CD scanning on Amazon Linux 2 operating systems (September 13, 2023).

quotes: #### September 13, 2023
ZPC provides support for scanning IaC files in the Bitbucket repositories.
You can install the Zscaler IaC Scan plugin on the JetBrains Integrated Development Environments (IDEs) and scan IaC templates.
ZPC provides support for IaC CI/CD scanning on Amazon Linux 2 operating systems.

bulk-actions-2022-12.statement: The December 08, 2022 note says actions (Resolve, Unresolve, Ignore or Unignore) can be performed on multiple alerts at once by selecting checkboxes on the Alerts table.

quotes: #### December 08, 2022
You can now perform actions (i.e., Resolve, Unresolve, Ignore, or Unignore) on multiple alerts simultaneously by selecting the checkbox on the Alerts table.

manual-remediation-2023-07.statement: The July 12, 2023 note says ZPC supports manual remediation of AWS alerts: single alerts, bulk alerts, or all alerts generated by a specific policy.

quotes: ZPC supports manual remediation of AWS alerts. You can remediate single alerts, bulk alerts, or all alerts generated by a specific policy.

ignore-end-date-2023-01.statement: The January 19, 2023 note says an Ignore filter can have an end date; when it passes, the Ignore status is removed and the alert returns to Open or Resolved depending on whether ZPC still detects the misconfiguration.

quotes: You can now define an end date for an Alert's Ignore filter.
When the date is passed, the Ignore status is removed from the alert and the alert returns to either Open or Resolved, depending on whether ZPC still detects the misconfiguration.

ignore-rule-invalid-2023-01.statement: The January 19, 2023 note says an icon appears in the Ignore Rule table when an ignore rule is no longer valid, and the rule is automatically disabled.

quotes: An icon indicating the ignore rule is no longer valid appears at the top-level Ignore Rule table, and the rule is automatically disabled.

ignore-options-2023-01.statement: The January 19, 2023 note says new ignore filter criteria include Cloud (an entire cloud service provider) and Policy Severity.

quotes: Cloud: Admins can ignore alerts for an entire cloud service provider, such as Amazon Webs Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Kubernetes.
Policy Severity: Admins can ignore alerts generated for Critical, High, Medium, and Low policy severities.

ignore-permissions-2023-08.statement: The August 17, 2023 note says the Add Ignore filter action is available by default to the Administrator and Security Operations roles, other ZPC users have view-only permission, and others can be given it through Ignore Rules permissions in Global Modules in custom roles; the Cloud Accounts attribute on the Filter Scope page is optional.

quotes: The Add Ignore filter action is now available by default to the Administrator and Security Operations (SecOps) role. All other ZPC users have view-only permission.
You can enable the Add Ignore Filter action for other ZPC users by adding or modifying Ignore Rules permissions in Global Modules using custom roles.
The Cloud Accounts attribute on the Filter Scope page is optional.

ignore-k8s-focus-2023.statement: Dated 2023 notes say Alert Ignore filters can filter on Kubernetes clusters and namespaces (May 17, 2023) and that the Policy Focus option selects whether the Ignore filter focuses on assets, identities or both (April 19, 2023).

quotes: Alert Ignore filters can now filter on Kubernetes clusters and namespaces.
The Policy Focus option selects if the Ignore filter focuses on assets, identities, or both.

compliance-ignore-2023-10.statement: The October 30, 2023 note says compliance ignore rules can be configured on combinations of policies, asset types, regions and accounts, and that ZPC does not display ignored compliance findings on compliance dashboards or reports.

quotes: You can configure compliance ignore rules based on a combination of policies, asset types, regions, and accounts.
ZPC does not display any ignore compliance findings on the compliance dashboards or reports.

compliance-score-2023-10.statement: The October 30, 2023 note says using compliance ignore filters can affect ZPC's compliance score evaluation, and that when you ignore or include an asset or policy the score might change.

quotes: dashboards or reports. Using compliance ignore filters can affect ZPC's compliance score evaluation. When you ignore or include an asset or policy on ZPC, the compliance score might change.

trusted-ip-2023-10.statement: The October 30, 2023 note says ZPC lets you upload a trusted IP list, and excludes those IPs when examining publicly exposed assets or identities.

quotes: ZPC allows you to create and upload a list of trusted IP addresses used by your organization to access the public environment.
ZPC excludes these trusted IPs when examining assets or identities that are publicly exposed

time-filters-2023-03.statement: The March 01, 2023 note says cloud alerts have two time range filters (Created Date and Updated Date) and IaC alerts have three (Scan Time, Created Date, Update Date).

quotes: Cloud alerts have two time range filters: Created Date and Updated Date.
IaC alerts have three time range filters: Scan Time, Created Date, and Update Date.

time-definitions-2023-03.statement: The March 01, 2023 note defines Created Date as the first time the misconfiguration is identified on the customer's public cloud, and Update Date as the most recent occurrence or the latest ZPC admin action on the alert.

quotes: The Created Date is the first time the misconfiguration is identified on the customer's public cloud.
The Update Date is either the most recent occurrence of the misconfiguration or the latest action performed by the ZPC admin on this alert.

alert-age-2023.statement: The March 01, 2023 note says Alert Age is the number of days since the last time the Alert Status was set to Open; the March 23, 2023 note says an Alert Age filter filters by exact age, older than or newer than an age, in days.

quotes: The Alert Age is the number of days since the last time the Alert Status was set to Open.
you can filter alerts by exact age, alerts older than a specific age, and alerts newer than a specific age. All ages are measured in days.

time-range-2022-10.statement: The October 13, 2022 note lists Time Range filter options including Last 12 hours and Custom Range.

quotes: Last 12 hours: View the alerts that were generated or updated in the last 12 hours.
Custom Range: View the alerts that are modified on the selected date range along with time.

azure-compliance-filters-2022-10.statement: The October 13, 2022 note says ZPC added Resource Group and Tags filters for Microsoft Azure compliance benchmarks.

quotes: Resource Group: Returns compliance benchmark details for a specific resource group.
Tags: Returns compliance benchmark information for assets with specific tags.

filter-management-2022-10.statement: The October 13, 2022 note says ZPC offers filter management: you can save a filter, and edit and delete a saved filter.

quotes: ZPC offers filter management. You can save a filter, and edit and delete a saved filter.

default-filters-2023-07.statement: The July 12, 2023 note says default filters are retained across revisits to the page and logout/login of the ZPC Admin Portal.

quotes: Default filters are retained so you can view customized data every time you revisit the page or when you log out and log back in to the ZPC Admin Portal.

alert-payload-2023.statement: Dated 2023 notes say alert payloads sent to integrations gained attributes: to cloud storage services AWS S3, Azure Blob and AWS Security Lake, Audit Procedure and Remediation (May 17, 2023); to Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, Splunk or AWS Security Lake, Audit Procedure, Remediation and Resource Metadata (July 12, 2023); to ITSM (Jira and ServiceNow), the same three (September 13, 2023).

quotes: #### September 13, 2023

Cloud and IaC alert payloads that are sent from ZPC to cloud storage services (AWS S3, Azure Blob, and AWS Security Lake) are enhanced to include additional attributes: Audit Procedure and Remediation.

Alerts sent from ZPC to the cloud storage service (Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, Splunk, or AWS Security Lake) are enhanced to include the following attributes: Audit Procedure, Remediation, and Resource Metadata.
Cloud and IaC alert payloads that are sent from ZPC to ITSM (Jira and ServiceNow) are enhanced to include additional attributes: Audit Procedure, Remediation, and Resource Metadata.

slack-2023-07.statement: The July 12, 2023 note says Slack integration is available for receiving ZPC alert notifications on Slack channels.

quotes: Slack integration is available. You can receive ZPC alert notifications on Slack channels

export-2022-10.statement: The October 13, 2022 note says Cloud or IaC alert data can be exported to an Excel file.

quotes: You can export the Cloud or IaC alert data to an Excel file and download the report.

remediation-attrs-2023-08.statement: The August 17, 2023 note says four remediation attributes and filters were added to the Cloud Alerts table: Supports Remediation, Remediation Allowed, Remediation Status and Remediation Initiated By.

quotes: Four new remediation attributes and filters are added to the Cloud Alerts table: Supports Remediation, Remediation Allowed, Remediation Status, and Remediation Initiated By.

eks-2022-12.statement: The December 08, 2022 note says ZPC supports onboarding AWS EKS clusters and gaining posture insight via the asset inventory.

quotes: #### December 08, 2022
You can onboard AWS EKS Kubernetes clusters and gain insight into their security posture via the asset inventory.

gke-aks-2023.statement: The January 19, 2023 note says ZPC supports onboarding GCP GKE clusters, and EKS and GKE clusters for multiple accounts in an organization; the March 23, 2023 note says Azure AKS clusters can be onboarded.

quotes: ZPC now supports Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters. You can onboard GCP GKE clusters and gain insight into their security posture via the asset inventory.
ZPC now supports onboarding EKS and GKE clusters for multiple accounts belonging to an organization.
You can onboard Microsoft Azure AKS clusters and gain insight into their security posture via the asset inventory.

aks-local-private-gke-2023.statement: The June 19, 2023 note says ZPC supports onboarding AKS clusters with local authentication, in addition to Azure RBAC and Kubernetes RBAC; the August 17, 2023 note says private GKE clusters can be onboarded.

quotes: In addition to AKS clusters authenticated by Azure RBAC and Kubernetes RBAC, ZPC supports onboarding AKS clusters with local authentication.
In addition to onboarding public and hybrid clusters, ZPC supports onboarding private GKE clusters.

k8s-enhancements-2023-04.statement: The April 19, 2023 note lists Kubernetes enhancements: metadata and posture for K8S IAM entities (roles, role bindings, service accounts), Kubelet configuration metadata, closing alerts for offboarded clusters, and a Warning status when metadata cannot be collected for certain services.

quotes: ZPC collects configuration metadata and offers security posture for K8S IAM entities such as roles, role bindings, and service accounts
ZPC collects configuration metadata for Kubelet configurations.
ZPC closes previously generated alerts for offboarded Kubernetes clusters.
ZPC displays a new status called Warning when it's unable to collect configuration metadata for certain services.

oci-limited-2023-06.statement: The June 19, 2023 note lists OCI support under Feature in Limited Availability: onboarding OCI cloud accounts and visibility of OCI posture in the Cloud Asset Inventory.

quotes: Feature in Limited Availability
Onboard your OCI cloud accounts on ZPC.
Gain visibility of your OCI infrastructure's security posture on the Cloud Asset Inventory.

ec2-exposure-fix-2023-04.statement: The April 19, 2023 note says EC2 instances connected to a subnet with a default subnet-ACL and a public ID were not detected as publicly exposed, and that this is now corrected and as a result a higher number of publicly exposed instances may be observed.

quotes: EC2 instances connected to a subnet with a default subnet-ACL and a public ID were not detected as publicly exposed.
This is now corrected and as a result, a higher number of publicly exposed instances may be observed.

gcp-functions-2022-10.statement: The October 13, 2022 note says ZPC supports GCP Functions as an identity in the IAM module when calculating an entitlement path.

quotes: ZPC now supports GCP Functions as an identity in the IAM module when calculating an entitlement path.

onboarding-status-2023.statement: The April 19, 2023 note says the Cloud Accounts page shows onboarding and configuration metadata collection status; the January 19, 2023 note says ZPC monitors the state of every account, organization and Kubernetes cluster.

quotes: The Cloud Accounts page offers visibility into onboarding and configuration metadata collection status.
ZPC now monitors every account, organization, and Kubernetes cluster's state.

cloud-accounts-2023-06.statement: The June 19, 2023 note gives cloud account Excel export file names as Cloudaccounts_<timestamp>, Cloudaccounts_organizations_<timestamp> and Cloudaccount_kubernetes_<timestamp>, and adds an Onboarded Date column.

quotes: Cloud Accounts: Cloudaccounts_<timestamp>
Organizations: Cloudaccounts_organizations_<timestamp>
Kubernetes: Cloudaccount_kubernetes_<timestamp>
The Cloud Accounts page displays a new column called Onboarded Date for each cloud account.

public-exposure-2023-05.statement: The May 17, 2023 note says publicly exposed assets get a visual indication in the Assets drawer and Assets table and a filter.

quotes: ZPC now shares a visual indication for publicly exposed assets in the Assets drawer and the Assets table, and includes a filter to search for such assets.

cve-predicates-2022-10.statement: The October 13, 2022 note lists new predicates for custom security policies and investigations including CVE Security (Critical, High, Medium, Low or Unknown), CVE Age (days since first published) and Vulnerability Fix Available (True or False, based on NVD).

quotes: CVE Security: The security level of the vulnerability (i.e., Critical, High, Medium, Low, or Unknown).
CVE Age: The number of days since the CVE was first published.
Vulnerability Fix Available: The vulnerability fix availability based on the NVD database (i.e., True or False).

asset-property-2023.statement: The August 17, 2023 note says the asset property predicate investigates AWS assets by any key-value pair in asset metadata, with array, multiple and partial value matching; the October 30, 2023 note adds Included In and Not Included In operators for IP address and integer property types.

quotes: ZPC supports the asset property predicate which offers the ability to investigate AWS assets based on any key-value pair in the asset metadata. ZPC accommodates for array, multiple, and partial value matching.
The asset property predicate supports two new operators for IP address and integer property types: Included In (⊆) and Not Included In (⊈).

tags-local-identities-2023.statement: The July 12, 2023 note says investigations and custom policy queries support all cloud-provider-supported tags; the September 13, 2023 note says AWS local identities are supported in investigation and custom policy queries.

quotes: #### September 13, 2023
ZPC supports all cloud service provider supported tags in the investigation and custom policy query creator.
ZPC supports AWS local identities in the investigation and custom policy query creator.

container-investigation-2023.statement: The May 17, 2023 note says container workload investigation uses Kubernetes asset properties and images used by AWS EKS workloads; the June 19, 2023 note says running containers (as opposed to idle or stale ones) and publicly exposed containers can be identified, and results exported as an Excel file.

quotes: You can create investigations based on Kubernetes asset properties and images used by AWS EKS workloads.
You can identify running containers as opposed to idle or stale ones and detect publicly exposed containers.
Kubernetes container investigation results can now be exported as an Excel file.

custom-policy-edit-2022-09.statement: The September 06, 2022 note says custom policies can be edited and deleted: editing the query closes existing alerts and generates new ones, and deleting a custom policy closes all its alerts.

quotes: #### September 06, 2022
When you edit the query, existing alerts are closed and new alerts are generated based on the new custom policy query logic.
When you delete a custom policy, all alerts generated by the policy are closed.

policy-catalog-2023.statement: The March 01, 2023 note says a disabled security policy is not run against collected configuration metadata; the January 19, 2023 note adds a Focus column showing whether a policy is asset focused or identity focused.

quotes: When disabled, the policy is not run against the collected configuration metadata.
Focus: View whether the security policy is asset focused or identity focused.

asset-risk-level-2023-01.statement: The January 19, 2023 note says Asset Risk Level is Low, Medium, High or Critical, based on the number and type of open alerts on the asset.

quotes: The Asset Risk Level shows an asset's risk level based on the number and type of open alerts associated with the asset. The Asset Risk Level is Low, Medium, High, or Critical.

audit-logs-2022-12.statement: The December 08, 2022 note says ZPC supports audit logs recording session information for every administrator who signs in to the ZPC Admin Portal, as a chronological list of activities in tenants onboarded to ZPC.

quotes: #### December 08, 2022
ZPC now supports the audit logs feature and records session information for every administrator who signs in to the ZPC Admin Portal.
The audit logs provide a chronological list of activities performed by users in the tenants that are onboarded to ZPC.

audit-logs-modules-2023-01.statement: The January 19, 2023 note says audit logs integrate with the vulnerability management and KSPM onboarding modules.

quotes: Audit logs now integrate with additional ZPC modules (vulnerability management and KSPM onboarding)

custom-roles-2022-10.statement: The October 13, 2022 note says custom roles can be added, edited or deleted, with permissions set for access to specific modules in the ZPC Admin Portal.

quotes: You can add, edit, or delete custom roles and set permissions for users to access or manage specific modules in the ZPC Admin Portal.

rbac-2023-07.statement: The July 31, 2023 note says administrators can be part of multiple groups including SSO groups, roles and business units are defined separately, and business units are mapped to groups.

quotes: ZPC now supports the ability for administrators to be part of multiple groups including single sign-on (SSO) groups.
now customers can define roles and business units separately. Business units are now mapped to groups.
Existing administrators need not make any changes, as all the roles and permissions are updated to the new model.

api-2023-06.statement: The June 19, 2023 note says ZPC supports REST APIs for code-based alert retrieval, requiring an API key created and managed in the ZPC Admin Portal.

quotes: ZPC supports REST APIs that allow for code-based alert retrieval. API access requires an API key, which you can create and manage in the ZPC Admin Portal.

api-correlation-2023-07.statement: The July 12, 2023 note says internal server errors return a correlation ID in an optional response header and the response body.

quotes: Internal server errors return a correlation ID in an optional response header and the response body to support troubleshooting.

last-login-2023-07.statement: The July 12, 2023 note says the Administrators page displays each administrator's last login time to the ZPC Admin Portal.

quotes: ZPC provides additional information by displaying the last login time of each administrator on the Administrators page.

system-notifications-2023-05.statement: The May 17, 2023 note says that at that time ZPC displayed system notifications for cloud account onboarding and data collection failures.

quotes: Currently, ZPC displays system notifications for cloud account onboarding and data collection failures.

executive-reports-2023.statement: The August 17, 2023 note says Executive Reports can be customized and shared in PDF format; the September 13, 2023 note says they can be scheduled for regular distribution to specified recipients at a specified frequency.

quotes: #### September 13, 2023
You can customize the report and share the report in PDF format.
You can schedule executive reports for regular distribution to specified recipients at the specified frequency.

identity-types-2023.statement: The March 01, 2023 note says a ZPC proprietary ML algorithm determines cloud identity types as human or non-human with more precision; the September 13, 2023 note says ZPC aligns with each cloud provider's classification of identities as human and non-human.

quotes: #### September 13, 2023
The ZPC proprietary ML algorithm can now determine cloud identity types as human or non-human with more precision.
ZPC aligns tightly with how each cloud service provider classifies identities as human and non-human.

cloud-identities-2023-07.statement: The July 12, 2023 note says the Cloud Identities page offers complete metadata, power score, authentication methods and open alert count.

quotes: The Cloud Identities page now offers complete metadata, power score, authentication methods, and open alert count.

limited-availability-outcome.title: Whether Azure Linux scanning and OCI support became generally available
limited-availability-outcome.detail: The September 06, 2022 note marks Azure Linux vulnerability scanning as limited availability and the June 19, 2023 note lists OCI support under Feature in Limited Availability; the captured release notes hold no later note that changes either status.

policy-and-service-tables.title: Which security policies and service coverage the notes added
policy-and-service-tables.detail: The notes carry long tables of added security policy titles (AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI, Kubernetes) and Improved Service Coverage service names that are not recorded as claims here; policy catalog or asset-type coverage needs the Security Policies and Cloud Asset Types articles.

unstated-values.title: Scan duration, operators and identity-type ML accuracy
unstated-values.detail: The release notes give no value for scan duration, and do not define the Included In and Not Included In operators or the accuracy of the identity-type ML.

undescribed-dated-entries.title: Dated entries in the 2022 and 2023 notes not recorded as claims
undescribed-dated-entries.detail: Not every dated entry is recorded here. Unrecorded entries include September 27, 2023 Ignore Compliance Filters (the feature the compliance-ignore notes cite), September 13, 2023 Alert Timeline, March 23, 2023 New Alert Attributes, October 13, 2022 Remediation Procedure in IDE/CLI and June 19, 2023 Amazon Security Lake; the captured pages are the source for each.

time-filter-names.title: Scan Time versus Scan Date for IaC alerts
time-filter-names.detail: The March 01, 2023 note lists IaC alert time filters as Scan Time, Created Date and Update Date, while its definition paragraph says 'The Scan Date is the last time the alert was set to open', and cloud alerts use Updated Date where IaC uses Update Date. The captures do not say whether the October 13, 2022 Time Range options remained after the March 2023 filters.
